title: Weather Nobody Wrote Down
question: How can we know what Earth's climate was like before anyone measured it?
hook: Weather records cover only about 150 years, yet one ice core holds clues stretching back over 800,000 years.
idea: Ice, sediments, cave rock and other proxies keep traces of past climate, and dating them lets scientists rebuild climate history long before instruments.

beats.prompt: A scientist drills ice from deep in an Antarctic ice sheet and carefully releases the gas trapped inside. What can she learn from it?

choices.label: What the air was made of when that ice formed
Only what today's air is made of
choices.feedback: The gas was sealed in as the snow turned to ice, so it is old air, not modern air.

choices.label: Nothing, since ice holds no trapped gas
choices.feedback: Air in fallen snow ends up encased in tiny bubbles as the snow is compressed into ice.

choices.label: How deep the ocean was that year
choices.feedback: The bubbles hold a sample of the air itself, not a reading of the ocean's depth.

beats.explain: Trapped air allows direct measurement of the air's composition from the time the ice formed.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in the order they happen as air gets locked into glacier ice
items: Snow falls, with air caught inside it
Later years' snow piles on top
The weight presses the snow into ice
The air ends up sealed in tiny bubbles
beats.explain: Air in fallen snow becomes encased in bubbles as the snow is compressed into ice under the weight of later snow.

beats.prompt: Match each record to what scientists analyse in it
beats.explain: Each archive keeps a different trace: ice traps air and pollen, lake cores build up sediment layers, and speleothems grow as rock formations.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Climate data only started being recorded in the mid-1800s.
That gives researchers about 150 years of measurements.
So those measurements alone can map a region's climate 10,000 years ago.
To look further back, researchers turn to sources such as ice cores.
beats.explain: About 150 years of records cannot reach 10,000 years into the past, which is why more complex methods such as ice cores are used.
